newsitem.title: USA: Guangdong would consider unit spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong would consider unit spinoff.

text.p: Guangdong Investment Ltd Deputy General Manager Zhen Tang said the company would consider spinning off some of its numerous subsidiaries as part of its strategy for future development.
Speaking at the Flemings-sponsored Asia '96 Investors Conference in New York, Zhen Tang said, "We would consider a spinoff of some well-established subsidiaries in the future."

Tang said the diversified holding company's development strategies include focusing on its five core business areas and continuing to focus investments in southern China's Guangdong province, one of the fastest growing and most developed areas of China.

He said about 95 percent of the company's investments in China are in Guangdong province and emphasized that investment in the province's infrastructure is extremely important to the company in the future.

Guangdong's core investments are in industry, infrastructure, travel/hotels, property and wholesale/retail, Tang said. Infrastructure, industry and travel/hotel make up about 94 percent of Guangdong's investment portfolio based on first half 1996 operating figures.

Managing Director Chen Dazhi said he believes contributions from both infrastructure and property development will grow in coming years, and said residential development is a promising business for the company. He said he also expects the travel/hotel segment to grow steadily and to continue benefiting from mainland China's development.

Guangdong is increasing production capacity at some industrial subsidiaries, Tang said. He said that it is doubling capacity at its Xushou unit and also boosting production capacity at both its Nanhau Cement Plant and its Shenzhen Brewery Co.

Guandong will finish the first stage of its third phase of expansion at the Shenzehen Brewery by the end of 1997, adding 200,000 tonnes of production capacity, according to the Deputy General Manager. Added capacity at its Yangcheng and Ninghu malting plants will also be available ahead of schedule, he said.
Guangdong Investment is 33.78 percent owned by Guandong Enterprises Ltd.
